ops.does: Back to Alex's first words. However they came, they're checked before any answer: the general danger check, plus the plug-in's own danger words.
more: The general check looks for danger to life, fire, gas, a medical emergency or self-harm.
The plug-in adds a resident's emergencies: a gas smell, smoke, or an alarm going off.
It also adds flooding, no heat in freezing weather, and a lockout.
Every answer later in the booking is checked the same way.
On a call, the voice AI says any safety words out loud.

ops.does: No search and no booking. The AI shows the safety words first. On a call, Rosie says them aloud, and Sam gets the call summary.
more: Say a resident writes: there's a gas smell in my unit. That's 911 first, then the emergency line.
Flooding, no heat in freezing weather or a lockout get the emergency line now, and nothing is booked.
A lockout with a child or a pet inside is 911 first.

say.text: This sounds like an emergency. If anyone is in danger, or you smell gas, leave and call 911 now. Then call {{biz.name}}' emergency line, {{biz.phone}}.
say.plainText: This sounds like an emergency. If anyone is in danger, or you smell gas, leave and call 911 now. Then call {{biz.name}}' emergency line, {{biz.phone}}.

ops.does: Some questions Rosie may not answer, like lease terms or a rent deal. They get the leasing office's own line, from Sam's settings.
more: Sam set this line at sign-up: the number for what only a person at the leasing office should answer.
911 or 988 come first when they're needed.
Applications and screening questions go to the leasing office's own process.
A disability accommodation request always goes to a person, never decided by Rosie.
These words don't stop a booking. Alex can go on and book a tour.

say.text: That's a question for the leasing office itself. {{pro.name}} can go over it at your tour. For anything sooner, call {{biz.name}} at {{biz.phone}}. For an emergency at home, call {{biz.phone}}.

steps.title: Checks for words that would steer
steps.does: Next, every message gets the fair housing check. Rosie answers everyone the same way. It never steers anyone toward or away from a home or an area.
more: It never asks about or comments on any trait the fair housing rules protect.
Those include race, color, religion, sex and national origin.
They also include disability, and family or children.
It gives no view of schools, crime or 'good areas'. Leasing agents follow the same rule.
Alex's question has none of these, so the answer goes on.

A single chirp every minute or so is a low alarm battery: a repair is booked.

ops.does: Nobody is booked into danger. A gas smell, smoke or an alarm going off gets 911 first. Flooding, no heat in freezing weather or a lockout gets the emergency line now.

The emergency line is the business's own, set at sign-up: (555) 010-0199.
On a call, the caller hears it, and Sam gets the call summary.
Nothing is booked by text for any of these.
